title: Provide better errors when parsing fails.
description:
It took me a while to figure out what I had a typo in one of my cpp functions. `cpp11::cpp_register` would fail with a cryptic error:

```
> decor::parse_cpp_function("raws C_encode(int 1, strings) { }")
Error in decor::parse_cpp_function("raws C_encode(int 1, strings) { }") : 
  negative length vectors are not allowed
```

title: Errors when parsing function declarations with comments
description:
I have tried various forms of using comments in argument declarations. But all of them fail.

This one
```c++
[[cpp11::register]]
int test_comments(int a, // = 5
                  int b) {
    return 0;
}
```
gives `Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : negative length vectors are not allowed`

This one
```c++
[[cpp11::register]]
int test_comments(int a /* = 5 */) {
    return 0;
}
```
gives
```
Error in parse(text = lines, srcfile = srcfile(file), keep.source = keep.source) : 
  /XXXXX/cpp11.R:15:27: unexpected '/'
14: 
15: test_comments <- function(/
                              ^
```

Would be nice to support comments, especially since specifying the default argument values is not implemented.

title: parse_cpp_function fails with spaces after fn name
description:
Sorry to lump you with more :bug::bug::bug:s @jimhester, but this one should be easier to fix that [yesterday's](https://github.com/r-lib/decor/issues/3#issuecomment-756039700). Note the only difference in the two `cpp_function` definitions below is that the second one has a space (so `test_cpp ()`, rather than `test_cpp()`).

``` r
decor::parse_cpp_function (c ("[[cpp11::register]]",
                              "double test_cpp() {",
                              "    return 1.0;}"),
                           is_attribute = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   name     return_type args            
#>   <chr>    <chr>       <list>          
#> 1 test_cpp double      <tibble [0 × 3]>

decor::parse_cpp_function (c ("[[cpp11::register]]",
                              "double test_cpp () {",
                              "    return 1.0;}"),
                           is_attribute = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   name  return_type     args            
#>   <chr> <chr>           <list>          
#> 1 ""    double test_cpp <tibble [0 × 3]>
```

<sup>Created on 2021-01-07 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

The name is not captured in the second case, and is in fact mashed on over with the `return_type`. This is unsurprisingly  quite consequential, and causes completely unintelligible errors when running `cpp11::cpp_register()` on functions defined like that second one.

---

Aside from that, this is all because it seems that `cpp11` has finally reached a stable enough state for me to start all new packages as `cpp11` rather than `Rcpp`, for which I am much indebted to you!! My initial motivation is because of compilation times of Rcpp packages with large code bases, but ultimately it's anticipation of `cpp11` being more readily extendible into exciting new C++20 realms. Awesome work!!!

title: Register fails with const reference parameters, where `&` is right-aligned
description:
Decorated functions of the following form parse incorrectly, prefixing the parameter name with the reference operator.
```cpp
[[cpp11::register]] void foo(const cpp11::integers &x) {}
```

The parsed args from the above result in (from [decor::parse_cpp_function](https://github.com/r-lib/cpp11/blob/master/R/register.R#L143)):
```
# A tibble: 1 x 3
  type                  name  default
  <chr>                 <chr> <chr>
1 const cpp11::integers &x    NA
```

I've traced this to decor [parse_arguments](https://github.com/r-lib/decor/blob/master/src/parse_cpp_function.cpp#L115-L121); splitting type and name by white space.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: `cpp_decorations` does not respect C++ comment blocks
description:
This has the following effect in `cpp11`:



``` r
f1 <- '#include "cpp11/doubles.hpp"
using namespace cpp11;

/*
[[cpp11::register]]
double mean_cpp(doubles x) {
  int n = x.size();
  double total = 0;
  for(double value : x) {
    total += value;
  }
  return total / n;
}
*/'
writeLines (f1, "src/f1.cpp")
cpp11::cpp_register ()
readLines ("src/cpp11.cpp")
#>  [1] "// Generated by cpp11: do not edit by hand"                                     
#>  [2] "// clang-format off"                                                            
#>  [3] ""                                                                               
#>  [4] ""                                                                               
#>  [5] "#include \"cpp11/declarations.hpp\""                                            
#>  [6] ""                                                                               
#>  [7] "// f1.cpp"                                                                      
#>  [8] "/* double mean_cpp(doubles x);"                                                 
#>  [9] "extern \"C\" SEXP _LTN_mean_cpp(SEXP x) {"                                      
#> [10] "  BEGIN_CPP11"                                                                  
#> [11] "    return cpp11::as_sexp(mean_cpp(cpp11::as_cpp<cpp11::decay_t<doubles>>(x)));"
#> [12] "  END_CPP11"                                                                    
#> [13] "}"                                                                              
#> [14] ""                                                                               
#> [15] "extern \"C\" {"                                                                 
#> [16] "/* .Call calls */"                                                              
#> [17] "extern SEXP _LTN_mean_cpp(SEXP);"                                               
#> [18] ""                                                                               
#> [19] "static const R_CallMethodDef CallEntries[] = {"                                 
#> [20] "    {\"_LTN_mean_cpp\", (DL_FUNC) &_LTN_mean_cpp, 1},"                          
#> [21] "    {NULL, NULL, 0}"                                                            
#> [22] "};"                                                                             
#> [23] "}"                                                                              
#> [24] ""                                                                               
#> [25] "extern \"C\" void R_init_LTN(DllInfo* dll){"                                    
#> [26] "  R_registerRoutines(dll, NULL, CallEntries, NULL, NULL);"                      
#> [27] "  R_useDynamicSymbols(dll, FALSE);"                                             
#> [28] "}"
```

<sup>Created on 2021-01-06 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

And that all happens because the [first call to `decor::cpp_decorations()`](https://github.com/r-lib/cpp11/blob/master/R/register.R#L42) returns the attributes, even though they're commented-out. Current `cpp_decorations()` function goes straight from [`readLines` to `grep(cpp_attribute_pattern...`](https://github.com/r-lib/decor/blob/master/R/decor.R#L60-L62), but needs to exclude block comments in between.

I've got some code elsewhere that does the messy work, if you want me to PR here. Comments can be constructed **and nested** in any conceivable way, requiring parsing of potentially nested sequences. The following will work at a line-level, but may not work perfectly for complex intra-line nesting (but who'd do such a thing???):

``` r
get_cmt <- function (sym = "\\/\\*", lines) {
    cmt <- gregexpr (sym, lines)
    lens <- vapply (cmt, length, integer (1))
    line_num <- rep (seq (cmt), times = lens)
    cmt <- unlist (cmt)
    cbind (line_num, cmt) [cmt > 0, ]
}

nested_sequences <- function (opens, closes) {
    i2 <- seq_along (opens) [-1]
    i1 <- i2 - 1
    index <- which (opens [i2] <= closes [i1])
    if (length (index) > 0) {
        for (i in index)
            opens [i + 1] <- opens [i]
        opens <- opens [-index]
        closes <- closes [-index]
    }
    list (opens = sort (opens, decreasing = TRUE),
          closes = sort (closes, decreasing = TRUE))
}

remove_cpp_comments <- function (lines) {
    cmt_start <- get_cmt ("\\/\\*", lines)
    cmt_end <- get_cmt ("\\*\\/", lines)
    cmts <- nested_sequences (cmt_start [, 1], cmt_end [, 1])
    cmts <- unlist (lapply (seq_along (cmts$opens), function (i)
                            seq (cmts$opens [i], cmts$closes [i])))
    lines [-cmts]
}

remove_cpp_comments (readLines ("src/f1.cpp"))
#> [1] "#include \"cpp11/doubles.hpp\"" "using namespace cpp11;"        
#> [3] ""
```
